newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gore calls on Japan to spur domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: Gore calls on Japan to spur domestic demand.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Monday called on Japan to achieve economic growth led by domestic demand, a Japanese official said.

In a meeting with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Gore also urged Japan to take "new approaches" to solve bilateral trade disputes over aviation and port practices, said the official who briefed reporters on the meeting.
Hashimoto replied that his government is now carrying out fiscal and financial reforms, which are expected to have favourable effects on the economy, the official said.
Hashimoto was quoted as saying Japan will make sure that its economic growth will be led by domestic demand.
Gore repeated U.S. demands that Japan agree to Washington's call for "open skies" -- the dropping of all restrictions on airline operations except for safety requirements, the official said.

Hashimoto said Japan will carry out aviation liberalisation step by step. "We cannot agree to the U.S. idea of open skies... Japan will carry out aviation liberalisation step by step," he was quoted as saying.
Japan has asserted that imbalances in the existing aviation treaty signed in 1952 must first be addresssed.
Hashimoto called on the U.S. to scrap its plan to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports, the official said.

The U.S. Federal Maritime Commission, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory practices at Japanese ports, said last month it would slap $100,000 surcharges from April 14 on vessels of Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK every time they stop at a U.S. port.
Gore was quoted as saying only that improvement in the nation's labour practices at ports would benefit Japan.
